proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is a specific legal power — the right to dispose of, consume, or destroy a thing — that attaches to a property-owner by virtue of their ownership status. It is externally grounded in the legal system's recognition of dominium rather than in any intrinsic physical property of the owner. This makes it a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Disposition. Because it is a legally conferred entitlement it is properly a subclass of LegalRight (itself already typed as a Role subclass in the working ontology), narrowing the genus to the specific facet of ownership concerning alienation and destruction. 'Abusus' names a kind (a category of legal right found across Roman-law systems), so it is a class rather than an individual.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of LegalRight (the right of disposal/destruction) within the classic Roman tripartite analysis of dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). LegalRight is already typed BFO_0000023 Role in the working ontology, so this subclass link preserves the BFO typing via inheritance.
Explicit typing assertion to BFO_0000023 (Role) ensuring HermiT can verify the BFO parentage directly on the class without relying solely on inheritance through LegalRight.

open_questions: Should Abusus be further distinguished into subkinds, e.g., Alienatio (transfer to another) vs. Consumptio/Destructio (physical destruction), given that Roman jurisprudence sometimes treated these separately?
Should the complementary facets Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right of fruits) also be introduced as sibling subclasses of LegalRight now, for completeness of the dominium triad?

Is the intent to model Abusus as a class of roles that any owner-individual can instantiate, or as a specific historical Roman legal category (which might call for an individual representing the Roman-law concept)?
Should a 'DomainOfProperty' or 'PropertyOwnership' role class be introduced as a parent between LegalRight and Abusus to represent full dominium, of which abusus is a part (BFO_0000050)?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus, the ius abutendi of Roman property law, denotes the power of an owner to alienate, consume, or destroy the thing owned. In BFO terms it is externally grounded — it exists only because a legal system recognises and confers it upon the bearer of dominium — which places it firmly in the Role (BFO_0000023) branch of specifically dependent continuants. It is not a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because its ground is social-institutional rather than intrinsic to the bearer. It is classified as a class (common noun denoting a kind) rather than an individual, since 'Abusus' names a category of legal right that can be instantiated by many particular right-tokens in many legal systems descended from or influenced by Roman law. The most natural placement within the working ontology is as a subclass of the already-present LegalRight class, which is itself a subclass of BFO_0000023, thereby preserving full BFO typing through inheritance while adding an explicit rdfs:subClassOf BFO_0000023 assertion for reasoner transparency.
